Switching from Windows to Mac rarely involves software limitations. Not only can the platform run all the top computer applications, but there are also countless practical applications that are exclusive to Mac.

The only major exception is gaming. However, the latest tests show that Windows games perform better on Mac than ever before, whether through official or unofficial channels...

Apple has a dedicated game porting toolkit designed to help developers evaluate how their Windows games perform on Mac, thereby encouraging and facilitating them to port games to the Mac platform.

However, according to Macworld's Filipe Esposito, this tool has also been used by players to run Windows software unofficially on Mac. He is one of them and says the latest test version brings a leap in performance, citing Grand Theft Auto V as an example.

I tested the Game Porting Toolkit 4 beta for several days on a MacBook Pro with an M4 Pro chip and found that the performance improvement fundamentally changes the experience of running demanding Windows games... Using the same M4 Pro MacBook Pro with 24GB of memory, with the same game settings and benchmarks, GTA V jumped from about 106 fps on GPTK 3 to about 176 fps on the GPTK 4 beta, an increase of about 66%. The game ran smoothly at 2K resolution with medium to high graphics settings.

He admits that not every game will see such significant improvements, but hopes these improvements will encourage game studios to see Mac as a viable platform.
